Context & provenance

About this edition.

The fourth part of the Book of Tribulations of Hanbal b. Ishaq (d. 273 AH), nephew and student of Ahmad b. Hanbal: reports about the Dajjal and the trials before the Hour.

The edition

  • TextKitāb al-Fitan of Ḥanbal ibn Isḥāq
  • CompilerḤanbal ibn Isḥāq (d. 273 AH)
  • EditionDar al-Basha'ir al-Islamiyya, Lebanon, 1st ed., 1419 AH / 1998 CE
  • Editor'Amir Hasan Sabri
  • Kind of workFascicle (juz')
  • DatingThe date shown is the death year of Hanbal b. Ishaq, 273 AH, not a verified date of composition.
  • Extent51 narrations

How the text is presented

Structure

An undivided fascicle of numbered reports. The first report gives the chain through which the part was transmitted; the reports after it begin from Hanbal’s own teacher.

English translation

The English is the supplied translation, which follows the source record by record. Notes that the translation attaches to a report appear beneath it, apart from the Arabic and English text.

Arabic text

The Arabic is the text of the source page records, shown as supplied. A report’s printed number stands in its label instead of the text, and page markers are carried over from the source.

Isnad and matn

The English chain and words are divided as the translation gives them. The Arabic is divided at the same point by a fixed rule that does not alter the text; where the rule finds no clean division, the Arabic is shown whole.

Transmitters

Transmission paths list the names the translation gives for each chain, in English only. No transmitter is identified beyond the wording of the source.

Completeness

The supplied source holds reports 1 to 50, and all of them are translated here. The translation notes that the source text it was given broke off after report 50.
